In Minecraft, the first tree is always felled by hand.
The hiss of a creeper is the requiem every player least wants to hear.
Diamonds only wait for you on layer 11; anywhere else is a lie.
Building a home is harder than defeating the Ender Dragon, because you'll never think it's good enough.
The End Portal needs Eyes of Ender, but if you aim wrong, all your work is wasted.
Netherite armor is ugly, but it really won't burn away.
Redstone technology makes me feel like a real engineer, even though it often explodes.
The iron golem in a village is the only one who unconditionally protects you.
When you dig down to bedrock, you suddenly realize the world has an end.
Endermen are terrified of water, yet they always bother you when you're repairing your house in the rain.
With a Silk Touch pickaxe, you can take a bee nest home and keep bees.
A fishing rod can not only catch fish, but also pull monsters off cliffs.
A simple wooden door can stop zombies, but not your griefing friend.
Piglins will attack if you stare at them for three seconds, so it's best to wear a golden helmet.
Chorus fruit can teleport you, but it might just send you into the void.
Building a Nether hub can save you half your real-life travel time.
The blue fire on soul sand never goes out, just like your love for this game.
A shulker's missile makes you levitate, and falling to death is one of the most frustrating ways to die.
Name a sheep 'jeb_' with a name tag, and it turns into a rainbow sheep.
The beam from a beacon can be seen from far away – that's the direction home.
Building a simple automatic farm keeps you fed forever.
The banner at a Pillager Outpost is every village's nightmare.
Taking on the Wither with an enchanted golden apple is a testament of courage and wealth.
Boats are the fastest vehicle when you ride them on ice.
Foxes will fight with a sword in their mouth – so cute.
Fireworks paired with elytra make you the king of the sky.
The 'pop' sound when a sponge absorbs water is so satisfying.
Obsidian needs a diamond pickaxe, but it's even more vulnerable to a ghast's fireball.
A composter is great for getting rid of excess seeds, and it produces bonemeal.
Wandering traders usually sell useless stuff, but their two llamas are adorable.
With slime blocks and pistons you can make a launcher that prevents fall damage.
A turtle shell gives you water breathing, but you have to wait for the baby turtle to grow.
Once a conduit is activated, you become superhuman underwater.
Soul Speed enchantment makes you dash across soul sand, but the book is hard to find.
Using a grindstone to remove enchantments is more eco-friendly than making a new tool.
A loom lets you design banners – each pattern is your signature.
A smoker cooks meat twice as fast as a furnace – essential when you're hungry.
A blast furnace smelts ore quickly, but you can't bake potatoes in it.
A stonecutter makes all kinds of stone bricks more efficiently than a crafting table.
Putting a book on a lectern acts as a bulletin board in multiplayer.
The fletching table is currently useless except as a job site.
The smithing table is the sacred block that upgrades diamond gear to netherite.
Placing an anvil next to a grindstone gives you both repairing and renaming.
Lanterns look better than torches, but they need iron nuggets – too expensive early on.
Soul lanterns give off a blue light, great for spooky builds.
Sea lanterns are the best light source underwater, and they're beautiful.
End rods can be placed upside down – a top choice for ceiling decoration.
Right-clicking grass with a shovel creates a path, perfect for garden trails.
Snow golems throw snowballs, but they're useless against most monsters – only good for pranks.
Name a vindicator 'Johnny' with a name tag, and it will attack all mobs except illusioners.
Rabbits are hard to hit, but their feet can make potions of leaping.
Polar bears look docile, but never approach their cubs.
Dolphins lead you to treasure, but remember to feed them raw cod.
A bee will die within seconds after stinging you – don't provoke them.
Pandas are neutral, but they get happy if you give them bamboo.
Strays (skeleton variants) shoot arrows of slowness – annoying.
Husks don't burn in sunlight, but they turn into ordinary zombies.
Drowned wield tridents and can even take yours from you.
When a guardian's laser locks onto you, you can hide behind a block to dodge it.
An elder guardian gives you mining fatigue, making breaking blocks painfully slow.
Shulkers hide in End Cities – killing them takes skill.
You can deflect a ghast's fireball back with a sword – test your reflexes.
Magma cubes jump high, but the big ones still go down in a few hits.
A blaze's shooting rod is its weak spot, but it's hard to aim at.
Wither skeletons drop wither skeleton skulls, a key ingredient to summon the Wither.
Zombified piglins (formerly zombie pigmen) roam the Nether in groups – never accidentally hit one.
Hoglins attack you, but you can drive them away with crimson fungus.
Striders are boats on lava – you need a warped fungus on a stick to steer them.
Pillagers' crossbows have piercing – hiding behind a shield won't save you.
A ravager can break through your walls, but you can block its attacks with a shield.
An evoker's fangs go through walls – super annoying, but it drops a totem of undying.
Vexes are tiny flying mobs – hard to hit and infuriating.
Illusioners create clones and cause blindness – the rarest of the illagers.
Witches drink potions to heal themselves and throw poison and weakness.
The trader's two llamas spit at you – try not to get hit.
The killer rabbit is a rare variant with extremely high damage – don't be fooled by its cuteness.
Giant zombies only occasionally spawn on hard mode – high health and damage.
When a charged creeper explodes, it makes nearby mobs drop their heads.
A skeleton trap horse appears during thunderstorms – approach it and lightning strikes, spawning four skeleton horsemen.
Zombie horses can't currently be tamed – spawnable only with commands.
A mule is a cross between a horse and a donkey – it can carry a chest.
Carpets on a llama are just decorative – no real effect.
Parrots imitate the sounds of nearby mobs, but never feed them cookies.
Bats have no drops – they're just for atmosphere.
Squids suffocate on land, but you can move them in a water bucket.
Glow squid ink makes glow item frames, so you can see items in the dark.
Axolotls help you fight underwater monsters and can be picked up in a bucket.
Goats ram you – they might even knock you off a cliff. Be careful on slopes.
Salamander? No, axolotls are the cutest underwater helpers.
Frogs eat small magma cubes and then drop froglights.
Tadpoles grow into frogs – they need water and time.
An allay helps collect dropped items – give it an object and it follows you.
The Warden (Sculk Shrieker's beast) comes after hearing three vibrations – run, don't fight.
If a sculk shrieker is triggered too many times, it summons the Warden – don't dig recklessly.
Echo shards can craft a recovery compass to help you find your death spot.
Placing torches around a monster spawner is the easiest noob-proof way to stop spawns.
On top of the Nether's bedrock ceiling, you can explore infinitely – but you need an ender pearl to break through.
You can respawn the Ender Dragon with boats and End Crystals, but don't break the crystals carelessly.
Defeating the Wither drops a Nether Star, which is the core of a beacon.
A beacon pyramid needs diamond blocks, emerald blocks, etc. – the full 4-layer pyramid requires 164 mineral blocks.
A simple redstone clock automates your farm's harvesting.
Using pistons and observers, you can make a fully automatic sugarcane farm and harvest while AFK.
The best way to get villager discounts is to cure zombie villagers – trades can go down to 1 emerald.
Trade for emeralds, then use them to buy gear from other villagers – that's the economic cycle.
Finally, remember: Minecraft is not about defeating the Ender Dragon, but about everything you build and all the memories you leave behind.
